executive_summary: The retro-pattern-extraction backlog drain (hourly cron, scripts/extract-pending-retro-patterns.mjs) processes retrospectives oldest-first without regard to how long ago the underlying event happened. When it drains a batch of sibling SDs (orchestrator children created on the same historical day) that share one common defect, each sibling gets recorded against its own distinct sd_id, which defeats /learn's single-SD noise-filter guards (scripts/modules/learning/filter.mjs) -- all three are keyed on first_seen_sd_id === last_seen_sd_id, so a pattern touching N SDs reads as N independent, genuinely recurring occurrences. A PLAN-phase TESTING review measured the 4 motivating patterns' actual site data and found the sites do NOT share one parent_sd_id or a narrow recording window (7-8 distinct parents each, windows from 5 minutes to 22 hours) -- ruling out a parent+proximity predicate. What the data DOES show cleanly: every single resolved site SD, across all 4 patterns, is status='completed'. The fix generalizes checkSingleSDClosedSource's existing single-SD-and-closed logic to multi-SD-and-ALL-closed: a pattern whose every referenced source SD has since completed is not evidence of an ongoing, active problem, regardless of how many distinct SDs it touched. Separately, lib/learning/class-escalation.js's mergeSite() stamps a site's first_seen at cron-processing wall-clock time rather than the retrospective's real historical created_at, misleading any human reviewer reading a pattern's history -- kept as a secondary, independent fix (deliberately NOT read by the primary fix, avoiding the destructive coupling a proximity-window design would have had with it).

functional_requirements.title: Generalize the single-SD-closed-source guard to ALL-sources-closed
functional_requirements.description: scripts/modules/learning/filter.mjs's checkSingleSDClosedSource (line ~122) currently fires only when pattern.first_seen_sd_id === pattern.last_seen_sd_id AND that one SD's status is in closedStatuses. PLAN-phase measurement against the 4 motivating patterns' real metadata.sites[] data ruled out a parent_sd_id+proximity-window predicate (sites span 7-8 distinct parent_sd_id values and 5-minute-to-22-hour windows, not one shared parent in a narrow window) -- see risks/PRD-history for the ruled-out design. The correct, data-supported predicate: derive the full set of DISTINCT sd_ids referenced by a pattern's metadata.sites[] array (not just first_seen_sd_id/last_seen_sd_id), resolve each one's status, and reject the pattern as closed-source noise when EVERY distinct sd_id resolves to a closed status (same closedStatuses set already used today) -- regardless of how many distinct SDs are in that set. checkSingleSDStaleOpenSource and checkSingleSDRetroLikeCategory are single-SD-shape-specific by design (they reason about ONE open SD's staleness, or ONE retro-like category's single-SD shape) and are NOT generalized by this SD -- only checkSingleSDClosedSource's closed-check is extended to the multi-SD case, since 'every referenced SD is closed' is a predicate that scales cleanly to N sites while 'this one open SD looks stale' and 'this one retro-like pattern needs 2+ distinct SDs' do not have an analogous N-SD generalization that this investigation has evidence for.
acceptance_criteria: fetchPatternSourceSDStatuses (scripts/modules/learning/filter.mjs, line ~481) is extended to also collect every sd_id present in each pattern's metadata.sites[] array (in addition to the existing first_seen_sd_id/last_seen_sd_id collection), so their statuses are available to the guard

checkSingleSDClosedSource is extended (or a new sibling function is added and wired into filterPatternsForLearning at the same call site) so that a pattern whose metadata.sites[] resolves to 2+ distinct sd_ids, ALL of which are in closedStatuses, is rejected -- matching today's behavior for the N=1 case exactly (no regression for existing single-SD-closed patterns)
A pattern with 2+ distinct sd_ids where at least one resolves to an OPEN status is NOT rejected by this guard (falls through to the existing checkSingleSDStaleOpenSource/other checks as today)

A pattern whose metadata.sites[] is absent, empty, or contains no resolvable sd_ids falls back to today's exact first_seen_sd_id/last_seen_sd_id-only behavior (no metadata.sites[] dependency introduced for patterns that never had rich site data)
The severity bypass (SINGLE_SD_SEVERITY_BYPASS, critical/high patterns exempted) is preserved and applies identically to the generalized multi-SD case

The 4 real patterns that motivated this SD (PAT-LES-8fb5175dce26, PAT-LES-15c6ed980a2e, PAT-LES-752e6a374f67, PAT-LES-e02af6e8e18d -- all severity=medium, all sites status=completed) are, when run through the fixed filter with their real recorded metadata.sites[], correctly rejected as closed-source noise

functional_requirements.title: Thread the retrospective's real created_at through to mergeSite's first_seen
functional_requirements.description: lib/learning/class-escalation.js's mergeSite(metadata, site, now = new Date()) stamps a new site's first_seen using cron-processing wall-clock time when no opts.now is supplied. Add an optional occurred_at parameter to IssueKnowledgeBase.recordOccurrence (lib/learning/issue-knowledge-base.js) that flows through recordSiteAndMaybeEscalate's opts.now (lib/learning/class-escalation.js). The correct call site is scripts/auto-extract-patterns-from-retro.js's extractPatternsFromImprovements (declared ~line 197; the recordOccurrence call is at ~line 245) -- NOT extractPatternsFromRetrospective (a wrapper that fetches the retro and dispatches into extractPatternsFromImprovements). Pass retro.created_at as occurred_at at that call site. extractPatternsFromImprovements also has a second write path, kb.createPattern (~line 271), used when NO similar existing pattern is found (a brand-new pattern's first occurrence) -- this path lets the DB default issue_patterns.created_at to now() with the same historical-vs-processing-time mismatch. Extend createPattern (or its caller) to accept and pass the same occurred_at so a brand-new pattern mined from an old retro is not itself born with a falsely-fresh created_at. Must be additive/optional throughout: lib/rca/rca-orchestrator.js's two real-time call sites (~line 319, 382, both inside module-private upsertIssuePattern, reachable only via exported processTriggerEvent) call recordSiteAndMaybeEscalate with 3 positional arguments and no opts object today -- confirmed by direct read this makes them byte-identical by construction once opts.now is additive, since they never pass a 4th argument.
acceptance_criteria: A synthetic retrospective fixture with an old created_at, run through extractPatternsFromImprovements (the update/recordOccurrence branch), produces a recorded site whose first_seen equals the fixture's created_at, not the test-execution time

A synthetic retrospective fixture with an old created_at whose content matches no existing pattern (forcing the createPattern branch) produces a new issue_patterns row whose created_at reflects the fixture's created_at, not the test-execution time

If retro.created_at is missing, null, or fails Date.parse (NaN), the extraction falls back to today's exact behavior (current wall-clock time) rather than throwing -- mergeSite's unguarded now.toISOString() must never receive an invalid Date

lib/rca/rca-orchestrator.js's real-time gate-failure and handoff-failure call paths are unchanged -- confirmed via their existing call signature (3 positional args, no opts) requiring no code change at all in that file
Existing callers of recordOccurrence that omit occurred_at (all pre-existing call sites) produce byte-identical output to before this change

functional_requirements.title: Verify no downstream consumer breaks
functional_requirements.description: lib/rca/rca-orchestrator.js's two recordSiteAndMaybeEscalate call sites (inside module-private upsertIssuePattern, reachable only via exported processTriggerEvent) and any other production caller of recordOccurrence/recordSiteAndMaybeEscalate must continue to function identically. Because no existing test suite currently imports or exercises upsertIssuePattern directly (confirmed: tests/unit/rca-skip-governance.test.js and tests/unit/rca-trigger-quick-wire.test.js cover adjacent functions, not this one), add at minimum one direct test through the exported processTriggerEvent entry point that exercises the real-time site-recording path, OR explicitly document the call-signature argument (3 positional args, no opts, hence unaffected by construction) as the verification method if a full integration test is judged disproportionate -- do not leave this FR's evidence resting solely on unrelated tests passing.

lib/rca/ existing test suite passes unmodified in assertions

risks.risk: RULED OUT DURING PLAN (recorded for history, not a live risk): a parent_sd_id + recording-proximity-window predicate was the first design considered for FR-1. Direct measurement against the 4 motivating patterns' real site data found 7-8 distinct parent_sd_id values per pattern and recording windows from 5 minutes to 22 hours -- neither a shared parent nor a narrow window. That design would have fixed zero of the four motivating patterns and was replaced with the all-sources-closed predicate before EXEC began.
risks.mitigation: N/A -- design was corrected in PLAN before implementation; FR-1 now specifies the data-supported predicate directly.

risks.risk: Extending fetchPatternSourceSDStatuses to resolve every metadata.sites[] sd_id (not just first/last) could add meaningfully more strategic_directives_v2 rows to resolve per filter run on patterns with many sites.
risks.mitigation: The existing function already batches .in() lookups in pages of 100 and dedupes via a Set before querying -- extending its id-collection loop to also read metadata.sites[] reuses that same batching/dedup path, not a new query pattern.

risks.risk: Threading occurred_at through recordOccurrence's call chain touches a function with a production caller outside this SD's direct control (lib/rca/rca-orchestrator.js); an implementation mistake could silently change real-time RCA trigger behavior.
risks.mitigation: Confirmed by direct read that both RCA call sites pass exactly 3 positional arguments with no opts object, so an additive 4th-argument default cannot affect them without an active code change to that file (which this SD does not make). FR-5's verification requirement still applies as a positive check, not just an absence-of-change argument.

risks.risk: A malformed or missing retro.created_at, if not explicitly guarded, would reach mergeSite's unguarded now.toISOString() call as an Invalid Date and throw a RangeError -- silently swallowed by recordSiteAndMaybeEscalate's existing catch-and-warn, which would drop the site write entirely rather than falling back to current time.
risks.mitigation: FR-2/FR-4's explicit malformed-timestamp acceptance criteria and test scenario (TS-4b) require a safe fallback to current-time behavior rather than allowing the throw to propagate.

system_architecture.summary: Two independent, additive changes inside the existing retro-pattern-extraction call chain: (1) the /learn noise filter's closed-source guard generalizes from single-SD to all-distinct-SDs-closed; (2) the site-recording path gains an optional historical-timestamp parameter. Deliberately NOT coupled -- the closed-source predicate does not read timestamps at all, avoiding the destructive interaction a proximity-window design would have had with (2) rewriting those same timestamps.
